title: Creating an RDS Decoy in AWS

blocks.text: The Relational Database Service (RDS) in Amazon Web Services (AWS) is a web service that allows you to set up and host relational databases (MySQL or PostgreSQL) on the cloud. You can create RDS decoy databases (public or private) based on MySQL or PostgreSQL to lure adversaries that are looking for databases to disrupt services or steal data. Optionally, the credentials of the master user of the database along with the URL can be added to a landmine policy as a lure.
Zscaler Deception uses Amazon RDS's db.t3.micro instance type to create RDS decoys. To learn more about Amazon RDS instance types, refer to the AWS Documentation.
Before creating an RDS decoy in AWS, you must ensure that you have:

blocks.item: Configured the integration between AWS and Deception.
(Optional) Obtained the necessary CloudShell command for the deployment script using one of the following methods:
Automated Download Method
Manual Download Method
This only applies to the CloudShell-based deployment.
Go to Deceive > Cloud Deception > AWS > RDS.
Click Add Decoy.
See image.
The RDS Decoy window appears.
In the RDS Decoy window:
Name: Enter a name for the RDS database decoy.
Account ID: Select the Account ID associated with the AWS account in which you want to deploy the decoy.
Region: Select the AWS region in which you want to deploy the decoy.
Description: Enter a description relevant to the RDS database decoy.
Engine Type: Select a database type (MySQL or PostgreSQL) from the drop-down menu.
Engine Version: Select a supported version of the database engine from the drop-down menu.
Publicly Accessible: Enable if you want the decoy to be accessible to anyone. Otherwise, if it is disabled, access to the decoy is limited to internal adversaries.
Subnet Group: Enable to deploy the decoy in a subnet group belonging to an existing VPC, then enter the subnet group name.
VPC CIDR: Enter the address in CIDR format for the VPC where you want to deploy the decoy. If a VPC is not available, a new VPC is created. This option is available only if Subnet Group is disabled.
Subnet CIDRs: Enter the subnet IP address range in CIDR format for the VPC. This option is available only if VPC CIDR is configured.
See image.
Click Save.
Deploy the decoys based on the method used to configure the integration between AWS and Deception:
Terraform-based deployment
On the Cloud Deception - AWS page, go to Settings.
Locate the AWS account you added, and click the Download icon in the Actions column.
See image.
In the Terraform Deployment Steps window, click Download to download the necessary files.
See image.
A ZIP file containing all necessary files is downloaded to your system.
Extract the downloaded ZIP file and open the aws-decoys.tf.json file in a text editor.
Locate the backend block in the aws-decoys.tf.json file. Add your back-end details and save the file.
The following example shows a backend block of an S3 bucket-based Terraform back end:
{ "terraform": { "backend": { "s3": { "bucket": "your-terraform-state-bucket", "key": "deception/terraform.tfstate", "region": "us-east-1", "encrypt": true } } } }
Ensure that you use the same back end for all configurations relating to the same AWS account.
In the terminal, go to the extracted folder, and run the following command to create a new workspace:
terraform init && terraform workspace new <workspace_name>
Run the following command to deploy resources:
terraform apply
Review the plan, and confirm it by entering Yes when prompted.
The necessary resources are deployed, and a JSON file containing the details of the state is downloaded.
On the Cloud Deception - AWS page, go to Settings, locate the AWS account you added, and click the Upload icon in the Actions column.
See image.
Select the downloaded JSON file to update the status to the Deception Admin Portal.
CloudShell-based deployment
Sign in to the AWS Management Console as an administrator.
Click the CloudShell icon on the navigation bar to launch AWS CloudShell.
See image.
The AWS CloudShell window appears.
In the AWS CloudShell window:
Run the deployment script using the command obtained via the automated download method or manual download method.
Enter the option to deploy RDS database decoys and press Enter.
The deployment script detects the Account ID and deploys the RDS decoys to the selected regions.
See image.
If you want to add multiple RDS decoys to AWS, repeat Step 1 to Step 4 for each decoy and then deploy all decoys simultaneously.

Upon successful deployment, the RDS database decoy is added to AWS. The deployment status is indicated by the icon next to the name of the decoy in the RDS decoys table (Deceive > Cloud Deception > AWS > RDS) within the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal. In addition, the URI value is automatically generated and associated with the public RDS decoys during the subsequent health check. The URI value is also shown in the RDS decoys table. To learn how to configure lures using RDS database decoys, see Configuring Lures Using AWS Decoys.
